b2-105.title: The Street Dance Battle
b2-105.story: On Saturday, Max took Anna to a [[street dance]] event in a park in Kyiv. Someone had placed a huge [[boombox]] in the middle of the square, and the music was loud enough to shake the trees. First came a [[rap battle]], where two guys traded clever lines about cold coffee and late buses. Then a girl started a [[beatbox]] rhythm with nothing but her mouth and a microphone. Max's sister Sofia was already warming up for the [[dance battle]], since she had been practicing [[breakdance]] for months. Her opponent was a confident [[break dancer]] who spun on one hand and made the crowd scream. Sofia answered with a surprising mix of moves: a bit of [[flamenco]] footwork, a silly [[cha-cha-cha]] step, and a perfect freeze at the end. When someone in the crowd shouted for [[twerking]], she just laughed and kept to her own style. The judges couldn't decide, so they declared a tie, and the two dancers shook hands. On the way home, Anna admitted that she wanted to take lessons too.

b2-106.title: Festival Weekend
b2-106.story: Anna's grandparents live in a small town in the mountains, and this weekend the town was hosting its first [[jazz fest]]. On Friday, Grandpa tried to listen to the festival news, but the [[radio signal]] kept fading in and out. Finally, he caught a [[radio interview]] with the organizer, who promised a [[laser show]] over the lake on Saturday. Grandma, however, was more interested in her favorite [[radio drama]], which she never misses. Anna and Max, who had come to visit, decided to go to the [[night show]] by the water. The lights were amazing, and a crew from a [[travel show]] was filming the whole thing for TV. After that, the friends stayed for the [[late show]], a comedy set by local musicians. It felt like a live [[sketch show]], with jokes about rain, grandmas, and lost tickets. When they got home, Grandma was still awake, and she wanted to hear every detail.

b2-107.title: A New Film
b2-107.story: Lisa has been obsessed with a fantasy book series ever since Ira told her it was a [[must-read]]. The original copies sold out years ago, but last month a [[reprint]] finally appeared in the bookstore near her school. Now the studio has released a [[teaser]] for the film version, and the whole [[fandom]] is going crazy online. Lisa even writes [[fan fiction]] about the minor characters, and hundreds of people read it every week. On opening night, she and Ira went to the [[multiplex]] in a homemade [[cosplay]] of the two heroines. A woman in the lobby joked that Lisa walked like a [[top model]] in her long silver cloak. The movie was better than they expected, and the [[plot twist]] in the last ten minutes left the audience silent. Ira's dad filmed them in their costumes outside, so now they have a funny [[home video]] of the evening. Lisa says she will watch it again when the sequel comes out.

b2-108.title: Learning a Language
b2-108.story: At the start of the semester, Anna's English teacher handed out the [[syllabus]] and announced a project on everyday language. Anna chose to compare the way her grandparents talk with the way her friends text. Her grandparents speak a village [[dialect]], while Max and Lisa use so much online [[slang]] that Mama rarely understands them. Anna watched a video [[tutorial]] on how to record interviews and started asking questions. She found that some words have no exact English [[equivalent]], so she had to explain them with examples. In other cases, a simple [[synonym]] worked, but it often missed a small [[nuance]] of feeling. Her teacher also lent her an old [[paperback]] about word history, which showed how many English words come from [[Latin]]. The hardest part was the presentation, because it started with five minutes of [[small talk]] with a visiting teacher from Canada. Anna was nervous, but she made the guest laugh with a joke about her grandfather's favorite word. In the end, she got the highest grade in the class.

b2-109.title: Help with Math
b2-109.story: Taras had a geometry test on Monday, so Anna offered to help him on Sunday afternoon. He said he preferred [[algebra]], because numbers seemed easier than shapes. Anna started with a glass of water and dropped an ice [[cube]] into it to explain volume. Then she showed him a can of beans and asked him to measure the [[cylinder]] with a ruler. "Its [[radius]] is four centimeters and three [[millimeters|millimeter]]," Taras said proudly. Next, she asked him to draw an [[oval]] and a [[spiral]] without looking at the paper, which made them both laugh. Mama brought his cold medicine and reminded him that one tablet of 200 [[milligrams|milligram]] was enough. Before bed, he took an online quiz that claimed to measure his [[IQ]], and he announced that he was a genius. The next day, he got a B plus, which he called proof of his genius.

b2-110.title: University Life
b2-110.story: Anna is in her first year at university in Kyiv, and her history course is mostly online. Every week she logs in to the student [[portal]] to download the next [[module]] and check her grades. This month's topic was how the city changed at the turn of the [[millennium]]. To find old photos, Anna and Max visited the city [[archive]], where a friendly librarian brought out boxes of maps and an old [[atlas]]. The librarian, a quiet [[intellectual]] with thick glasses, seemed to know every street from memory. Meanwhile, Max was proud of his ninety-day [[streak]] in a language app, which he checked even in the reading room. Anna's project was chosen for the university exhibition, which carries some [[prestige]] in her department. At the end of the semester, she received a [[certificate]] with her name in gold letters. She gave a copy to the librarian to say thank you.

b2-111.title: Trouble at School
b2-111.story: Last month, a new boy joined Taras's class after moving back from Canada. At first, the language [[barrier]] made it hard for him to answer questions quickly. He loved computers and robots, so some classmates started calling him a [[geek]] as if it were an insult. One day, a few boys played a [[prank]] on him by hiding his backpack during the break. That evening, someone posted a photo of him online with the word "[[loser]]" on it, and Taras knew this was [[bullying]], not a joke. He showed the post to their teacher, who said that every online [[hater]] counts on other people staying silent. The next day in biology, she was explaining how a [[nerve]] sends signals to the brain, and she asked the new boy to help with the model. Then she talked to the class about how a [[stereotype]] can hide who someone really is. She said courage was the [[attribute]] she admired most, and she thanked Taras in front of everyone. By Friday, the new boy had joined the school robotics club, and Taras had joined it too.

b2-112.title: Grandpa in the Hospital
b2-112.story: In November, Anna's grandfather caught a bad cold that slowly turned into [[pneumonia]]. The doctors decided to keep him in the hospital for a week, and the nurses checked his [[pulse]] every few hours. Because of a flu outbreak, his ward was under [[quarantine]], so visitors could only talk to him by video call. The man in the next bed had spent two weeks in a [[coma]] after a car accident, but now he was sitting up and telling jokes. He said he was alive thanks to a blood [[donor]] he would never meet. That story impressed Anna so much that she decided to give blood as soon as she turned eighteen. Grandma, meanwhile, sent Grandpa bags of oranges, sure that [[vitamin]] C could cure anything. Grandpa laughed at her, but his [[optimism]] seemed to help more than any medicine. On Sunday, he came home, and the first thing he asked for was Grandma's soup.
